subject: Contract staple: addendum clarification for upcoming capacity uptick
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@orchidai.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@orchidai.com, Anya Volk <anya.volk@orchidai.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on Order Form v3 + section 5 carveouts

Hi Vivek & Laura,

Thanks for sending OrderForm v3 last night — we reviewed internally this morning. A few legal items popped up that will block signature unless we can align quickly:

1) MSA section 5 (Indemnity / Data residency): Orchid asks for a narrow carveout for regulated PII processing with a 60-day remediation window rather than the 30 days in your draft.
2) Billing proration: Procurement wants the first invoice prorated for the ramp (we're adding 4 incremental seats mid-quarter).
3) SLA credits: Can we confirm the calculation method for credits in Exhibit B?

I've attached Orchid's redline PDF for the MSA and an annotated billing spreadsheet from procurement. Can your legal team review and propose language? We're aiming to execute before the end of the month due to our planned product launch.

Attachments: Orchid_MSA_redlines.pdf (pdf, 12 pages), procurement_billing_notes.xlsx (xlsx)

Best,
Samir

Subject: Re: Questions on Order Form v3 + section 5 carveouts

Samir — thanks for the prompt review and the attachments. We're aligned on the priority and can move fast. Quick notes from product/sales side before legal writes language:

- Capacity ramp: we can prorate the first invoice for any mid-quarter seat adds; will confirm the exact proration formula with billing ops and put it in the order form appendix.
- SLA credits: we use the Exhibit B method (minutes-of-outage-based credit) but happy to add worked examples to avoid ambiguity.

Kimberly, would you take leads on section 5 redlines and propose a 60-day remediation alternative that protects Redwood (limiting consequential exposure) but meets Orchid's need? Jordan, please include the final proration formula in the order form appendix and I will review before routing.

Samir — we'll aim to have proposed language by Monday EOD (PST). If that timing works, I will circulate a consolidated orderform + redline back to your legal and procurement.

Thanks — Vivek

Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Samir Patel <samir@orchidai.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Draft counter-proposal for Section 5 (Indemnity / Data)

Hi all — I reviewed Orchid's redline and drafted targeted language that should be acceptable to both sides. Key points:

- Proposed compromise: Redwood accepts the 60-day remediation window proposed by Orchid for regulated PII, but only where the customer can demonstrate compliance obligations that require the extended window. Otherwise, the standard 30-day cure applies.
- Limitation: carveout is scoped to third-party regulatory obligations (HIPAA-equivalent) and excludes general security incidents; we keep standard indemnity caps and exclude punitive/consequential damages as in the MSA.
- Audit evidence: require the customer to provide a redacted compliance plan within 10 business days after execution to qualify for the extended window.

I've attached a pdf with inline markup (MSA_Section_5_counterproposal.pdf) and an excerpt we can paste into the order form. Jordan — I left a placeholder in the order form appendix for proration (see cell A12 in the attached spreadsheet).

Suggested next steps: 1) Samir confirm whether Orchid's legal can accept the evidence requirement; 2) we consolidate and send a single combined redline (MSA + OrderForm appendix) for signature.

Attachments: MSA_Section_5_counterproposal.pdf (pdf, 4 pages), orderform_proration_cellnotes.xlsx (xlsx)

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 11:09:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft counter-proposal for Section 5 (Indemnity / Data)

Thanks Kimberly — helpful and clear. A few clarifying Qs from Orchid legal: 

1) Evidence requirement: Orchid accepts providing a compliance plan, but can we instead commit to deliver it within 20 business days post-execution? Our internal signoffs run slower; 10 business days is tight.
2) Proration: procurement confirms they need the formula explicitly in the order form (net days and prorated daily rate). Can you paste a sample calculation so Procurement can approve?
3) SLA credits: we still need the worked example you mentioned for Exhibit B. Without that, procurement will push for a higher credit floor.

If you can address those three items in the combined redline, we can move to signature. Also — please send the DocuSign link for the orderform when ready so procurement can queue payment.

Best,
Anya Volk
General Counsel, OrchidAI
anya.volk@orchidai.com

Subject: Re: Draft counter-proposal for Section 5 (Indemnity / Data) — next steps and DocuSign

Anya / Samir — thanks for the quick replies and the flexibility. Summary and agreed path: 

- Evidence window: Redwood accepts 20 business days for the compliance plan delivery (per Anya's ask). We'll reflect that in the combined redline.
- Proration formula: Jordan will paste the explicit calculation into the OrderForm appendix (daily rate = annual committed seats / 365, prorated by start date). We'll include a worked example row; see attached orderform_proration_example.xlsx.
- SLA credits: Kimberly will add two worked examples to Exhibit B — one for a partial-day outage and one for a sustained outage — to make the calculation transparent.

Next steps: 1) Kimberly to produce combined MSA + OrderForm redline incorporating the three items above; 2) Jordan to update the orderform appendix with the proration formula and example; 3) Vivek will circulate combined redline and DocuSign link by EOD tomorrow so procurement can queue payment.
